Terminal PR review guide

ghui on Omarchy

A free, keyboard-driven terminal UI that puts all your open GitHub pull requests across every repo in one place.

Reviewed 2026-11-24 · independent editorial guide

Short answer

Install ghui with omarchy pkg add ghui, then run gh auth login once and ghui in any terminal. It needs the GitHub CLI installed and logged in, because ghui reuses gh's authentication. It is MIT licensed and free.

ghui on Omarchy

ghui is a free, keyboard-driven terminal UI that puts all your open GitHub pull requests across every repo in one place, so you can review diffs, leave comments, and merge without opening a browser.

TL;DR

omarchy pkg add ghui
gh auth login
ghui

That installs ghui v0.9.1-1 (~49.1 MB download, ~140.4 MB installed, MIT licence). It needs the GitHub CLI (gh) installed and logged in, because ghui reuses gh’s authentication and does its own login step.

Getting started (5 minutes)

1. Log in to GitHub first.

ghui has no login screen of its own. Before launching it, authenticate the GitHub CLI:

gh auth login
gh auth status

If gh auth status shows you logged in, ghui will work. If it does not, ghui has nothing to authenticate with.

2. Launch it from anywhere.

Run ghui in any terminal. It opens a dashboard of your open pull requests across repositories, with queues you switch between using Tab / Shift-Tab. Use j / k or arrow keys to move, Enter to expand a PR’s details, and r to refresh.

3. The 3 things you need to know:

  • Review a diff without leaving the terminal. Press d on a PR to see the stacked diff for all changed files, then use [ / ] to switch files and Enter on a line to start a comment. Press v to select a multi-line range for a comment.
  • Approve or request changes from the keyboard. Press Shift-R to open the review modal, choose Comment, Approve, or Request changes, and submit. Press m to merge, s to toggle draft or ready-for-review, and l to manage labels.
  • Check CI without opening GitHub. Press a on a PR to see its GitHub Actions runs for the head commit, drill into a run with Enter, and jump between failures with n / p.

Practical notes: Other keys worth learning: / to filter, o to open the PR in your browser, e to open it in your editor, y to copy PR metadata, Ctrl-P for the command palette, and q to quit.

Common issues & fixes

ghui opens but shows no PRs, or errors about authentication

ghui does not log you in itself; it needs gh authenticated.

Fix: Run gh auth status. If it says you are not logged in, run gh auth login and complete the browser flow, then relaunch ghui. If gh works but ghui still fails, check that the token gh is using has not expired or been revoked (re-run gh auth login to refresh it). Unverified on Omarchy: not tested with a live account for this guide. (ghui README)

The PR list stops updating, or requests fail with a rate-limit error

ghui talks to GitHub’s API through gh, and GitHub caps authenticated requests at 5,000 per hour per account, shared across every token and app acting for you. Heavy polling plus other tools can eat that budget.

Fix: Wait for the hourly reset (GitHub reports the reset time in the error), close other GitHub tools, and lower how much ghui fetches with GHUI_PR_FETCH_LIMIT (default 200) and GHUI_RUN_FETCH_LIMIT (default 20 per PR). (GitHub rate limits; ghui README)

Pressing e does nothing, or opens the wrong directory

The editor handoff needs a repoPaths entry mapping the repo to your local clone. Add it to ~/.config/ghui/config.json:

{
  "repoPaths": {
    "owner/repo": "~/code/repo"
  }
}

Fix: Without a matching entry, ghui cannot resolve a local path. You can also set a custom editorCommand template (for example, a tmux command that checks out the PR branch and opens your editor). See the README’s editor section for the full template variables. (ghui README)

The list is slow or shows PRs you do not care about

ghui fetches up to 200 PRs by default. If you follow many repos, that is a lot to pull on every load.

Fix: Lower the fetch limit for a faster load: GHUI_PR_FETCH_LIMIT=100 ghui. You can also put the values in a .env file (copy .env.example from the repo) instead of typing them each time. Unverified on Omarchy: fetch-limit behavior was read from the README, not timed on a real machine. (ghui README)

A PR you just opened, merged, or closed does not show the new state

ghui polls GitHub rather than receiving live updates, so state changes made in the browser or by someone else only appear after a refresh or a refetch.

Fix: Press r to refresh. If a refresh still shows stale data, quit and relaunch. Unverified on Omarchy: refresh behavior was read from the README keybindings, not tested live.

Pairs well with / If you hate this, try

Pairs well with

  • gh (the GitHub CLI, which ghui depends on), lazygit for the repo side of the same workflow, and your editor of choice via the e handoff (Neovim with diffview.nvim or octo.nvim is the documented recipe).

If you hate this, try

  • Stick with gh pr list and gh pr status in the terminal, which give you the same data as plain text and are scriptable. Or use GitHub’s web PR inbox if you prefer a mouse.

Verdict: If you live in the terminal and review PRs across many repos, ghui is the most complete keyboard workflow of the free options. If you only check PRs occasionally, gh pr list is enough and costs you nothing to learn.

ghui is a free alternative to paid PR-dashboard tools

ghui is a free alternative to paid PR-dashboard tools. Instead of a subscription tool that aggregates your pull requests, you get the same single-pane review queue for $0. What you give up: hosted notifications, a web dashboard you can open on your phone, and team analytics. What you keep: the full review workflow — diffs, inline comments, approvals, merges, CI status — in one keyboard-driven screen, with no account beyond the GitHub login you already have.

Frequently asked questions

Is ghui free?

Yes. It is MIT-licensed and free to install and use. The only requirement is a GitHub account and the GitHub CLI.

Do I need a separate GitHub login for ghui?

No. ghui reuses the GitHub CLI’s authentication. Run gh auth login once and ghui uses that token, including for GitHub Enterprise.

Does ghui work with GitHub Enterprise?

Yes. Because it authenticates through gh, it works wherever gh is authenticated, including GitHub Enterprise hosts. Unverified on Omarchy: Enterprise was not tested for this guide.

Where does ghui store its settings?

UI preferences live in config.json under GHUI_CONFIG_DIR if set, otherwise under the platform config directory, which is normally ~/.config/ghui/config.json on Linux. Fetch limits are environment variables: GHUI_PR_FETCH_LIMIT (default 200) and GHUI_RUN_FETCH_LIMIT (default 20).

Can I review PRs from many repos at once?

Yes, that is the point. ghui aggregates open PRs across repositories into one list, with queues you switch between using Tab / Shift-Tab.
